readings: Total the payment amounts for each rental, counting only payments linked to a rental and taking the store from the rented inventory copy. For each store, keep the rentals whose payment total is strictly greater than the average rental payment total computed once over all rentals from both stores together. Show the store id, the sum of those rentals' payment totals, and the average amount by which they exceed that single overall average. Averages ignore missing values. Do not round.
queries:
WITH rental_totals AS (
  SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM rental_totals
)
SELECT rt.store_id,
       SUM(rt.total) AS total_payment,
       AVG(rt.total - o.avg_total) AS avg_excess
FROM rental_totals rt
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE rt.total > o.avg_total
GROUP BY rt.store_id;
